event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: Because this 10-K was filed in February 2022—well within three years of the WHO’s March 2020 pandemic declaration—the Time Decay Principle allows relatively high risk scores.  IRM repeatedly discloses that COVID-19 has already harmed its service activity levels and revenue mix while also signalling that future impacts remain highly uncertain.  The language toggles between concrete, realised effects (lower Records & Data Management activity, reduced 2020 service operations) and broad, forward-looking threats (supply-chain disruption, remote-work cyber-risk, dependence on vaccine progress and variant trajectories).  Although no dollar amounts are quantified, management expressly links the pandemic to revenue headwinds, operational changes, labour/work-arrangement shifts and heightened cybersecurity exposure—each mapping directly to the analysis focus.  Mitigating language is limited to one sentence noting that digitisation trends have not accelerated because of COVID-19; overall tone is cautionary rather than reassuring.  Consequently, aggregate risk is assessed as elevated (but not maximal) recent-event exposure: the company is already absorbing adverse effects and warns these could intensify.  The evidence therefore earns mid-to-high severity micro-scores (4-7) where impacts are specific and current, moderate scores (3-4) for forward-looking uncertainty, and near-zero/negative where mitigating statements appear.

evidence_list.snippet: Our business, operations, and financial results have been, and could continue to be, impacted by developments in the COVID-19 pandemic.

components.reason: States realised impact on business, operations, and financial results (‘have been’).
Adds a clear forward-looking warning (‘could continue’).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Confirms both current and future exposure; generic but unequivocal, meriting a solid mid-level score.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic, and the ongoing emergence of variants of the SARS-CoV-2 virus, and the resulting actions taken in response by governments, businesses, and individuals have resulted in, and are expected to continue to result in, substantial  increased cyclical impacts to the global economy, including a curtailment of business activities (including changes in demand for a broad variety of goods and services), weakened economic conditions, disruptions in supply, manufacturing and logistics, economic uncertainty and volatility in the financial markets, both in the United States and abroad, as well as reduced service operations and changed business practices for us, our customers, and other third parties with which we do business.

components.reason: Links pandemic to substantial, already-occurring impacts (‘have resulted’).
Projects continuation of those impacts (‘are expected to continue’).
Enumerates multiple concrete impact domains: demand shifts, supply-chain, logistics, service operations.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highly detailed description of wide-ranging, continuing effects drives a high severity score.

evidence_list.snippet: Due to the unpredictable and rapidly changing nature of the COVID-19 pandemic, the extent to which it continues to impact us will depend on numerous factors that we are unable to predict and are not within our control, including: the duration or re-emergence of outbreaks and developments of variants of the SARS-CoV-2 virus, the distribution, public acceptance and efficacy of COVID-19 vaccines; the continuation, resumption, and/or expansion of restrictions imposed by governments and businesses; the impact of any resulting inflationary or recessionary conditions and general economic uncertainty in the global markets; the pace of economic recovery from any impact of the COVID-19 pandemic; and the impact of any such factors on our customers, suppliers, vendors, and other business partners.

components.reason: Highlights extreme unpredictability, signalling open-ended risk.
Lists multiple uncontrollable drivers (variants, vaccine uptake, restrictions, inflation).
Points to cascading effects on customers, suppliers and partners—broadening exposure.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Focuses on uncertainty and multiple risk drivers; important but less concrete, yielding a moderate score.

evidence_list.snippet: Our Records Management and Data Management service revenue growth is being negatively impacted by declining activity rates as stored records and tapes are becoming less active and more archival, and these activity levels were further negatively impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic.

components.reason: Describes ongoing negative impact on a specific revenue stream (‘service revenue growth is being negatively impacted’).
Explicitly attributes the additional decline to the pandemic.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct link between COVID-19 and reduced service revenue drives a high mid-range score despite lacking quantification.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, the continuation of remote work arrangements as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic has increased and could further increase our cybersecurity risks.

components.reason: Identifies a specific operational vulnerability (cybersecurity) worsened by pandemic-driven remote work.
Warns that risk could escalate further.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specific but narrower exposure (cyber risk) warrants a moderate score.

evidence_list.snippet: While our service operations have increased from the reductions we experienced during the first and second quarter of 2020, future service revenues remain uncertain and will be dependent on the severity of the COVID-19 pandemic, including new variants of COVID-19 that may emerge.

components.reason: States that future revenues remain uncertain and pandemic-dependent.
References potential new variants intensifying risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Emphasises forward-looking revenue uncertainty tied to pandemic trajectory; moderate severity.

evidence_list.snippet: To date, our customers’ shift from paper and tape storage to alternative technologies has not accelerated as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic.

components.reason: Indicates pandemic has not aggravated this particular trend, acting as a mitigating statement.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Provides counter-evidence that pandemic did NOT worsen one risk area, so overall contribution is neutral after mitigation.
